subject: Clarify CPRA service-provider boundary for runtime telemetry aggregates
messages:
From: Kate Liao <kate.liao@finserv.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: FinServ Legal <privacy@finserv.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Question on telemetry aggregates and SP boundary (CPRA)

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for the call yesterday. A few follow-ups from our privacy and engineering teams:

1) FinServ is concerned about the phrasing in the DPA that describes "telemetry and runtime usage aggregates" as covered by the service provider/processor exception under CPRA. Can you confirm whether the aggregates we receive (1) contain any persistent identifiers or can be re-linked to customer records, and (2) whether we would be considered a "recipient" for the purposes of "sharing" under CPRA if we export aggregated CSV telemetry for our engineering analysis?

2) They also want the subprocessor list and the proposed onshore fallback steps in the event an offshore subprocessor becomes unavailable for legal or compliance reasons.

3) Finally: deletion proof. If FinServ issues a governed deletion request for telemetry associated with a specific customer-id, what evidence will Redwood provide that aggregated telemetry derived from that data has been purged or re-aggregated?

We attached a short diagram showing the telemetry flows from our side — can you map back to Redwood's dataflow and proposed contract language?

Attachments: telemetry-flows-finserv.pdf (diagram)

Best,
Kate
Kate Liao
Head of Privacy Operations
FinServ Inc.
From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: Kate Liao <kate.liao@finserv.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Question on telemetry aggregates and SP boundary (CPRA)

Kate — thanks, forwarding to ops and privacy counsel for a detailed mapping. High level answers below so you have something to review with your team before we send a redline: 

- Aggregate telemetry: our runtime exports include pre-aggregated counters (token counts, p95 latency, model variant). Those exports do not include customer PII by default. However, some optional debug exports can include a hashed request-id; those are ephemeral and accessible only under support debug mode. We can disable hashed request-ids at your account level.

- Re-identification risk: the standard aggregates we propose (daily model-token tallies by tenant-id) are tenant-scoped. If you require stronger de-identification we can (a) remove tenant-id and use cohort-id, or (b) increase aggregation windows so individual sessions cannot be inferred.

- Sharing/sale: if you receive CSV exports of telemetry for your own account, that would not be a "sale" or "sharing" under CPRA provided the exports are strictly for your internal product/ops use and the DPA explicitly states the telemetry is collected and processed as a service provider on behalf of the controller. We will propose contract language that (i) restricts exports to account admins and (ii) limits onward disclosures to subprocessors that we list and the onshore fallback flow.

- Deletion evidence: we can support a three-part approach: (1) regenerate aggregates excluding deleted tenant records then compare hashes; (2) provide a signed attestation and timestamped deletion log; (3) for higher audit requirements, provide a CSV diff and a short replay showing the recomputed aggregates. We will include an SLA for deletion turnaround in the redline.

Attaching our internal telemetry map and a first-pass clause -- Laura / Aditya, see attachments and can you draft concrete DPA language and a subprocessor onshore fallback paragraph?

Attachments: redwood-telemetry-dataflows-v2.pdf, proposed-cpra-clause-draft.docx

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Senior Manager, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai, Kate Liao <kate.liao@finserv.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 08:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Question on telemetry aggregates and SP boundary (CPRA)

Kate — following up with proposed contract text below (first pass). I kept the wording focused on: (A) classification (service provider processing), (B) controls (de-identification + export limits), and (C) onshore fallback + subprocessor transparency. Please review and tell us which option you prefer for de-id.

--- PROPOSED CLAUSE (excerpt) ---
1) Telemetry and Aggregates. For clarity, "Telemetry" means runtime usage metrics and aggregates generated by Redwood in the course of providing services to Customer. Telemetry does not include Customer Content unless explicitly enabled by Customer in writing.

2) Service Provider Processing. Redwood processes Telemetry as a Service Provider on behalf of Customer. Redwood will not retain or use Telemetry for independent advertising or sell/share Telemetry except as needed to provide the contracted services or as required by law.

3) Export and Access Controls. Exports of Telemetry will be available only to Customer account administrators or as otherwise authorized in writing. Optional debug identifiers (hashed request-ids) may be disabled at Customer request.

4) De-identification and Deletion. On Customer deletion request, Redwood will (i) recompute affected aggregates excluding the deleted data within the agreed SLA window, (ii) provide a signed deletion attestation with timestamps, and (iii) deliver a delta report (CSV) demonstrating the recomputed values. For customers requiring cryptographic non-recoverability, Redwood will switch to cohort-only aggregates (no tenant or session identifiers) on mutually agreed terms.

5) Subprocessors and Onshore Fallback. Redwood will provide an updated subprocessor list at least 30 days prior to onboarding. If an offshore subprocessor becomes unavailable for legal/commercial reasons, Redwood will: (a) attempt to migrate processing to an onshore subprocessor within the 30-day window; (b) provide temporary onshore buffering in our US region; and (c) notify Customer with migration timeline and any interim impact to exports.

--- end excerpt ---

Aditya, can you add a short paragraph about the CSV export redaction steps and confirm we can produce the recomputed-delta report automatically?

Kate — if this aligns with your team's expectations, we can produce a redlined DPA including these paragraphs and the subprocessor appendix.

Laura Bennett
Director, Product Compliance
Redwood Inference
From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai, Kate Liao <kate.liao@finserv.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 16:40:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Question on telemetry aggregates and SP boundary (CPRA)

Kate / team — technical confirmation and small ops note:

- CSV export redaction: when Customer requests exports, our export pipeline applies tenant scoping, field-level redaction rules, and a final sampling guard if the export would expose small cell sizes (< 10). That prevents re-identification from sparse telemetry. We can make the small-cell threshold configurable by agreement.

- Recomputed-delta automation: yes — we can automate the recompute and create the delta CSV within the deletion SLA. The delta will include aggregate keys, prior value, recomputed value, and a hash of the recompute job id signed by our system key. We will put this artifact into a secure drive link for Customer retrieval.

- Subprocessor list: current subprocessors for telemetry processing are listed in the subprocessor appendix. Short list: US logging provider (onshore), EU analytics store (replicated, can be disabled), support debug partner (hashed ids only). We will push an updated appendix with the onshore fallback details and migration SLAs.

Next steps: Laura to produce the redline and we'll run the recompute demo against FinServ's sample telemetry. Priyom — can you schedule a 30-min technical walkthrough this week?

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior Product Manager, Observability
Redwood Inference
